NOW COME, John A. “Matt” Matthews, Jr. on behalf of KLM Griffin Ranch, L.P.;
William Reid Pfluger on behalf of the Pfluger Family Limited Partnership; Carolyn Quillen on
behalf of William Quillen, James Blake Quillen, and Quillen Family Partnership, Ltd.; and Carolyn
Quillen (hereinafter “Respondents”), and file this response to Link R1 Opposition Landowners’
Objections to and Motion to Strike Portions of Direct Testimony and Exhibits in the above-

referenced proceeding and respectfully show as follows:

This response is supported by the Affidavit of John A. “Matt” Matthews attached hereto as

Exhibit A and fully incorporated herein.

The objections are based upon the Texas Rules of Evidence, which generally apply in this
proceeding. However, said rules are not to be applied absolutely. Texas P.U.C. Rule of Procedure

§22.221 provides:

Page 1 of 5

 §22.221. Rules of Evidence in Contested Cases.

(a) Texas rules of evidence apply. The Texas Rules of Evidence as applied in nonjury civil
cases in the court of Texas must be followed in contested cases. Irrelevant, immaterial,
or unduly repetitious evidence must be excluded. When necessary to ascertain facts
not reasonably susceptible of proof under the Texas Rules of Evidence, evidence
not admissible under those rules may be admitted, except where precluded by
statute, if it is of a type commonly relied upon by reasonably prudent persons in
the conduct of their affairs.

{emphasis added].

The exhibits objected to here are true and correct copies of the records maintained by Mr.
Matthews in the Kickapoo Ranch’s business records and have been relied upon by him and the
Kickapoo Ranch for many years. (See Exhibit A). Mr. Matthews is not holding himself out as an
expert archeologist or hydrologist or lawyer. He is simply providing the Court with facts needed

to evaluate the proposed routes.

Texas Rule of Evidence 803 provides many exceptions to the rule that hearsay is

inadmissible, including:

T.R.E. 803(16) Statements in Ancient Documents. A statement in a document that is at least 20

years old and whose authenticity is established.

The exhibits sought to be excluded are authenticated by Mr. Matthews’ testimony (see Exhibit A)
and date back to 1975 — 1978 and 1984 and are therefore well beyond the 20 year definition of
ancient documents. Because this exception to the hearsay rule applies to Exhibits 2-33, they should

be admitted into evidence over the objections.

The following table addresses each objection individually.

BEFORE ME, the undersigned official, on this day appeared John A. “Matt” Matthews, Jr.,
who is personally known to me, and after first being duly sworn according to law under oath
deposed and stated:

"My name is John A. “Matt” Matthews, Jr.. I am over the age of 18 years, I am a resident of
Tom Green County, Texas and I am fully capable of making this affidavit. I have personal
knowledge of the facts stated herein and they are true and correct.

“I am the Manager of Merrick Davis Ranch Management, LLC, the General Partner
of KLM Griffin Ranch, L.P., the owner of Kickapoo Springs Ranch in Tom Green, Concho and
Menard Counties. As such, I am the custodian of the ranch records and am familiar with the
manner in which its records are created and maintained by virtue of my duties and responsibilities.

“Attached to my testimony in this case [Item 3876] as Exhibits 2-33 are 69 pages of records.

They are true and correct copies of the records that have been maintained in the business files of the
ranch since the records were created.

AFFIDAVIT OF JOHN A. “MATT” MATTHEWS, JR. Page | of 2

 “Exhibits 2-32 are site survey forms prepared by James H. Word with the Texas
Archeological Society — Balcones Research Center on the dates shown thereon from 1972 through
1978. For over 40 years, we have relied upon these records in order to protect these archeological
sites on the Kickapoo Springs Ranch.

“Exhibit 33 is a Groundwater Hydrology Report prepared by Camp, Dresser and McKee in
1984. For over 40 years, we have relied upon this report as we have taken action to protect the
springs and as we have designed and implemented plans to improve the water flow by removing
invasive plant species from the recharge zone and beyond.

“Further affiant sayeth not.
